slides.say: A, B and C represent digits. Given: A A A minus forty-six is equal to B C. B plus C is equal to what?
A subtraction, and look, the choices are letters too. [short pause] We'll solve it by flipping it into an addition.
[short pause] First, vertically. A subtraction is hard to read, so flip it. A A A minus forty-six is B C means B C plus forty-six is A A A.

Why does it help? Take A A minus B B equals B B. Flipped, it's B B plus B B equals A A. Now you see it at once, B is one, two, three or four. Five is too big, fifty-five plus fifty-five is one ten, three digits.
Back to ours. Two two-digit numbers, B C and forty-six, add up to a three-digit number. So the leading digit is one. A is one, and A A A is one eleven.

Some students go on digit by digit here. C plus six ends in one, so C is five, carry one, and so on. It's correct, but slow. Just calculate. One eleven minus forty-six is sixty-five. So B is six, C is five, and B plus C is eleven.
Now the choices are letters. A is one, so A A is eleven. Choice number three is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
